item.title: The Millionaire Who Vanished Into Mexico
item.description: Peter Chadwick was charged with killing his wife in 2012, then disappeared while awaiting trial after posting $1 million bail. He spent more than four years hiding in Mexico under aliases before a tip led authorities to his capture.

item.title: The Names Inside Jeffrey Epstein’s Birthday Book
item.description: A birthday book created for Jeffrey Epstein in 2003 contained personal messages from around 50 prominent figures, including Donald Trump, Bill Clinton, Alan Dershowitz and Leslie Wexner. The contents later drew renewed scrutiny over Epstein’s connections to powerful people.

item.title: She Vanished While Investigating Vampires And The Mob
item.description: Journalist Susan Walsh disappeared from her New Jersey home in 1996 after investigating Russian organized crime and New York’s underground vampire scene. She had also spoken about a stalker, but investigators never established a connection to any of the theories, and Walsh remains missing.

item.title: The Murder That Became One Of America’s Biggest Mysteries
item.description: Six-year-old JonBenét Ramsey was found dead inside her Boulder home on December 26, 1996, after her family reported a ransom note. Her death was ruled a homicide, and despite decades of investigation, the case remains unsolved.

item.title: How Japan’s Biggest Pop Mogul Hid His Abuse
item.description: Johnny Kitagawa built Japan’s most powerful male idol agency while allegations of sexual abuse followed him for decades. A 2023 independent investigation found he had sexually abused hundreds of boys, exposing a long-running failure by the entertainment industry and media to confront the claims.

item.title: Eminem Once Linked Diddy To Tupac’s Murder
item.description: Eminem referenced the long-running allegations surrounding Sean “Diddy” Combs and Tupac Shakur’s 1996 killing in his 2018 diss track “Killshot.” The lyric was framed as a taunt toward Machine Gun Kelly, while Diddy has denied involvement and has never been charged in Tupac’s death.

item.title: How Warnings Before Itaewon Were Missed
item.description: On October 29, 2022, 159 people died in a crowd crush during Halloween celebrations in Seoul’s Itaewon district. Authorities had received warnings about dangerous overcrowding beforehand, and subsequent investigations examined failures in prevention, crowd control and emergency response.

item.title: He Stayed Silent Until He Finally Confronted His Abuser
item.description: Clark Fredericks said he was abused as a child by Dennis Pegg, a respected Boy Scout leader and law enforcement officer. He remained silent for decades before confronting Pegg in 2012. Fredericks later pleaded guilty to manslaughter and became an advocate for abuse survivors.

item.title: Police Wrote Off The Missing Twins As Runaways
item.description: Fifteen-year-old twins Dannette and Jeannette Millbrook vanished in Augusta, Georgia, in 1990. Despite no history of running away, their disappearance was initially treated as a runaway case and later closed. The investigation was reopened in 2013, but the sisters remain missing.

item.title: How Zheng Shuang Went From Star To Outcast
item.description: Zheng Shuang was once one of China’s biggest young actresses, but her career collapsed in 2021 after a surrogacy controversy and accusations involving her children. Months later, authorities fined her 299 million yuan for tax evasion and banned her from broadcast productions.
